title: 7-Day Overwhelm Recovery
description: When everything feels like too much, start with one thing. This program helps you break through overwhelm and find your starting point.
outcomes: Find your first step when everything feels overwhelming
Break large tasks into manageable pieces

days.title: The Single Step
days.insight: Overwhelm happens when you see the mountain, not the first step. Your brain needs a clear starting point.
days.action: Identify ONE task that feels overwhelming. Write down the very first physical action required to start it. Then do that one thing.
days.reflectionQuestion: What's the smallest, most obvious first step?

days.title: The Two-Minute Rule
days.insight: If a task takes less than two minutes, do it immediately. This clears mental clutter and builds momentum.
days.action: Go through your tasks and complete all the two-minute items. Then look at the next item and ask: what's the two-minute version of this?
days.reflectionQuestion: What tasks have you been avoiding that take less than two minutes?

days.title: The Big Picture
days.insight: When overwhelmed, zoom out. Ask: what's the one thing that would make the biggest difference right now?
days.action: List all your tasks. Circle the one that, if done, would make everything else easier or clearer.
days.reflectionQuestion: What's the one thing that would make everything else easier?

days.title: Delegation or Deletion
days.insight: Overwhelm often comes from doing things that don't matter. Learn to say no or delegate.
days.action: Look at your tasks. Which ones can be delegated? Which can be deleted entirely? Write the emails or messages now.
days.reflectionQuestion: What am I doing that doesn't require my unique skills?

days.title: Time Blocking
days.insight: Overwhelm is often about unclear priorities. Time blocking creates clarity.
days.action: Take 30 minutes of your day and block it for one specific task. No exceptions. No distractions. Just do it.
days.reflectionQuestion: What do I actually have time for today?

days.title: The Reset
days.insight: When overwhelmed, sometimes the best move is to step away. Your brain needs space to reset.
days.action: Take a 15-minute break. No phone. No email. Just walk, breathe, or close your eyes.
days.reflectionQuestion: What would help me reset right now?

days.title: Progress Over Perfection
days.insight: You don't need to get everything done. You need to make progress. Done is better than perfect.
days.action: Look at what you've accomplished this week. Not what's left. Celebrate the progress, however small.
days.reflectionQuestion: What progress have I made that I'm proud of?
